skill.name: test-failing-test
skill.description: Runs a controlled Node test that prints stdout, stderr, and a simulated stack trace before failing.
skill.summary: Tests how agent environments display failing tool output.
skill.author: EnactProtocol

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no findings, and the JavaScript file only prints output, creates a simulated error, and exits. Manual review found one semantic concern: the skill metadata places user input inside a shell-style command template.

remediation.issue: User input is interpolated into a shell-style command.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the message through a structured argument API or apply the runner-approved escaping method before command execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Command Argument Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md embeds the message input directly in a shell-style command string. If the runner substitutes input before shell execution, quote characters could alter the command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command template includes user-controlled input on the command line. Exact exploitability depends on runner escaping, which is not visible in this skill.

content.value_statement: Developers need predictable failure output when testing agent tool handling. This skill prints stdout, stderr, and a simulated stack trace before exiting with an error.
actual_capabilities: Accepts an optional message string for the failure run.
Prints a start marker and the supplied message to stdout.
Writes error markers and stderr text before exiting.
Creates a simulated Error object and prints its stack trace.
Exits with status code 1 for failure-handling tests.
limitations: It is designed to fail on every run.
It does not run assertions or validate application behavior.
It does not capture logs from other tools or services.
Command argument handling depends on the skill runner environment.

use_cases.title: Agent Error Handling Checks
use_cases.description: Verify that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code displays tool stdout, stderr, and stack traces clearly.

use_cases.title: Pipeline Failure Visibility
use_cases.description: Run a predictable failing command to confirm logs and nonzero exits appear in automation.

use_cases.title: Support Reproduction
use_cases.description: Generate consistent failure output when documenting how an agent environment reports tool errors.

prompt_templates.title: Run Default Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the failing test tool with its default message and summarize the visible stdout and stderr.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for basic failure visibility.

prompt_templates.title: Use Custom Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the failing test tool with the message: Release check failure. Tell me which lines appear before the stack trace.
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm that custom messages appear in the captured output.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Output Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the tool and separate the stdout lines from the stderr lines in your response.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate how an environment labels standard output and error output.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Failure Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the tool with a unique trace label, then explain whether the environment preserved the label, stack trace, and failed exit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of end-to-end failure reporting behavior.

output_examples.input: Run the tool with the default message.
output_examples.output: The run starts, prints the default message, reports stderr output, shows a simulated failure, and ends with a nonzero exit.

output_examples.input: Run the tool with the message: Pipeline check.
output_examples.output: The output includes the custom message, standard output text, error output text, and a stack trace for the simulated failure.

output_examples.input: Separate the visible stdout and stderr content.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the normal progress lines separately from the error marker, stderr text, and simulated stack trace.

best_practices: Use short, non-sensitive messages because the message is printed to logs.
Run it only in test environments where a nonzero exit is expected.
Review stdout, stderr, and exit status separately when validating agent behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a real health check because it always fails.
Do not pass secrets or personal data in the message value.
Do not rely on it to validate application test suites or business logic.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It runs a Node script that prints stdout, prints stderr, shows a simulated stack trace, and exits with failure.

faq.question: Why does it always fail?
faq.answer: The failure is intentional. It helps users confirm that agent environments expose failed tool output clearly.

faq.question: Can I provide a custom message?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill accepts a message value and prints it before the simulated error output.

faq.question: Does it test my application code?
faq.answer: No. It only tests failure visibility for this controlled command.

faq.question: Should I include secrets in the message?
faq.answer: No. The message is printed to logs and should not contain secrets or personal data.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
